questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Whether it is too late to stop Arctic ice melting
How the coronavirus pandemic affected the climate
Record high temperatures in California
How satellites are built to study ice
questions.why: Georgina says they'll look at climate change in the Arctic and ask if it's too late to change.

questions.q: Why does Georgina say climate change has received less attention in 2020?
options: Scientists have stopped studying it
The ice has stopped melting
People believe it is already solved
The coronavirus has dominated the headlines
questions.why: She says with coronavirus dominating the headlines, attention has moved away from climate change.

questions.q: What do we learn about Greenland's ice sheet?
options: It is roughly the same size as the state of Texas
It holds enough water to raise sea levels by 6 metres
It is about 6 kilometres thick in the middle
It is growing a little bigger every single year
questions.why: Neil says it is three times the size of Texas and holds enough water to raise sea levels by 6 metres.

questions.q: According to Michalea King, what was the situation before 2000?
options: The ice sheet was growing quickly
The ice sheet was melting faster than today
Ice lost was roughly replaced by new snow
No one was measuring the ice
questions.why: She says the ice lost from glaciers was approximately equal to what was gained from snow each year.

questions.q: What is happening to the glaciers now?
options: They are shrinking faster than new ice forms
They are staying the same size
They are growing because of more snow
They are moving further inland
questions.why: Georgina says the glaciers are shrinking faster than new ice is being accumulated.

questions.q: What message does Michalea King want to send?
options: It is too late to do anything
The ice sheet will soon recover by itself
Only governments can make a difference
We can still slow the loss, so we shouldn't give up
questions.why: She says we can control the rate of mass loss and it's not a 'give up' kind of situation.

questions.q: What does Michalea King think will probably still happen?
options: The ice sheet will disappear this century
Ice loss will stop completely
The ice sheet will continue to lose mass
Sea levels will fall
questions.why: She says it seems likely that we will continue to lose mass, though a slow rate is preferred.

questions.q: How does Neil describe the overall message at the end?
options: Worrying, with no hope left
Positive, but everyone needs to act soon
Confusing, because scientists disagree
Unimportant compared with the pandemic
questions.why: He says it's a positive message but calls for everyone to do what they can before it's too late.
